title: STUDY TOPIC The Spirit in the life of Jesus part 11
devotional:
The Holy Spirits involvement in Jesus’ temptation in the wilderness.

It is very surprising what happened to Jesus after he experienced the Holy Spirit at his baptism. Mark tells us that ‘The Spirit then compelled Jesus to go into the wilderness.’ Mark 1:12.

It is as if Jesus as a man, needed to experience the life and work of the Spirit in his private and personal life before he could demonstrate the power of the Spirit through his ministry. This was a time of testing ordained by his Father, so Jesus could discover what it really meant to live in submission as a human son.

Or to put it an other way, the work of the Spirit in Jesus’ personal life was a means of continually affirming his identity. At his baptism, Jesus was declared as God’s son, in the wilderness, Jesus chose to act as God’s son and live out of his true identity.

Jesus was submitted to the Spirit.

As we have seen before. The word translated compelled is ekballo in Mark 1:12 is a very weak translation. The word he uses for “Sent” is an extremely strong word, it literally means to drive out your enemies. In the LXX [The Greek translation of the New Testament.] the word is used to describe how God cast Adam out of the garden of Eden see Genesis 3:34. it was also used in the context where an enemy, frustrating or standing in the way of God fulfilling his purpose for his chosen people, so they are ‘cast out’ by God, so that God’s purposes may be fulfilled. See Exodus 23:30 Deuteronomy 33:27ff.

We are not told how the Spirit did this. But as a man, Jesus made a conscious choice to submit his life to leading and control of the Spirit even though is was contrary to everything that felt right or comfortable.

The word for wilderness (eremos) means lonesome, solitary, uninhabited, uncultivated region. MacArthur adds that "the wilderness of Judea, where Jesus was most likely tempted, was the most barren, desolate region in all of Israel. Scarred by precipitous cliffs, deep ravines, and tumbled boulders, it was a region so barren that animals could not be pastured in it.

In this remote, largely uninhabited area, Jesus might be more alone than anywhere else in Israel. This particular desert was known as ‘Jeshimmon’ or "The Desolation." This stretch of land covers a 35×15 miles scarred plot of limestone waste between Jerusalem and the Dead Sea. It remains inhospitable and barren, incapable of sustaining human life.

I love the fact that Luke speaks about Jesus being loved by the Father before being led by the Spirit. Jesus knew that he was completely loved by his Father, and this gave him the security to be lead by the Spirit. Often as Christians we struggle with being Spirit led. Sometimes God may put something in our minds or hearts and we think, ‘I could never do that,’ or ‘is this really God?’ And we allow fear and insecurity to stop us. Be assured, if you feel you should pray with someone, or show some kindness to someone, make a sacrifice so you just bless someone, or just feel you should show them love and bring God’s grace to them, these feelings or desires are never of Satan.

We must not overthink or allow our insecurities to prevent us from acting. Knowing that God loves you, will give you the courage to follow the Spirit’s leading.

I think I have fallen into the trap of thinking, that the work of the Spirit in my life is more about ‘Eden,’ than the wilderness. I want God to place me in a garden, where I feel comfortable, safe, and secure, not in a howling wilderness where I feel exposed, vulnerable and out of control. Yet it’s in the solitude of the wilderness we discover that God our Father is enough. We need to get our head around the fact that sometimes when we are not in the wilderness we maybe outside the will of God! Sometimes people can think and talk about a ‘wilderness experience’ as if it were something that is bad, evil or even a consequence of sin. Now sometimes that can/may be the case. However, a ‘wilderness experience’ also can or may be the result of complete faithfulness and devotion to God.

It is amazing that if you read through Luke’s gospel you will notice that Jesus often withdrew to the ethmos, wilderness Luke 4:42, 5:16, 9:10 and sometimes to other places, 6:12, 9:18, 11:1 and 22:39. Although Jesus’ initial experience in the desert was extremely difficult, he developed a love for it because it was there were he could have a deeper relationship with his Father away from distracting noises and pressing responsibilities.
prayer: Father help me to accept the fact that sometimes the wilderness is completely in your will.
